problem: Existing EQA models (navigation planner + VQA module) assume clean labels and degrade under label noise, since EQA's multi-step reasoning makes it sensitive to noisy supervision.
motivation: EQA is intended for real applications such as home robots and personal assistants, where annotations are inevitably noisy. Robustness to label noise must be built in before deployment; the VQA and navigation parts each need noise filtering, and the whole system must be coordinated.
key_idea: A label-noise-robust learning framework for EQA that combines co-regularized joint training of two parallel VQA branches, two-stage (trajectory-level and action-level) filtering of navigation labels, and a joint robust learning mechanism that trains the whole system on purified labels.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that noise must be handled at each level (answer labels, trajectory labels, action labels) and that the modules should be coordinated using the purified labels, rather than applying a generic noise-robust loss.
method: Joint-training co-regularization for VQA: two parallel network branches are trained with one loss function, with co-regularization used to filter noisy VQA labels.
Two-stage hierarchical robust learning for navigation: noisy navigation labels are filtered first at the trajectory level, then at the action level.
Joint robust learning mechanism: the purified labels are used as inputs to coordinate training of the whole EQA system (navigation plus VQA).

setting.backbone: EQA navigation planner + VQA module (specific architectures not stated in the abstract)
setting.training_data: EQA training data with synthetically injected label noise (20% and 45% noisy labels); exact dataset not stated in the abstract
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (assumed from standard EQA; not stated in the abstract)

results: The abstract states that under extremely noisy (45% noisy labels) and low-level noisy (20% noisy labels) settings, models trained with the proposed algorithm are more robust than existing EQA models. No numbers are given.
limitations: Evaluated on synthetic label noise, at 20% and 45% noise rates only.
Full details on the dataset, simulator, and baselines could not be verified from the abstract alone.
